title: QuoteChaser: instant replies and follow-up for B2B quotes and leads
source: Top 25 SaaS ideas for Victor (research report, Nov 2026)
summary: Replies to new B2B leads within a minute and follows up open quotes with AI-written messages until the buyer says yes or no.
hook: "We sent the quote, the buyer went quiet, and nobody followed up. We found out a month later they bought elsewhere."
story:
**Sara runs a B2B Shopify store selling packaging to cafés and shops.** Her "request a quote" form brings in dozens of requests a month. She or her one sales rep replies when they have time, often the next day, and follow-ups happen only when someone remembers.

When she exports the last 90 days of quotes, a big share never converted and most got **no second message**. With QuoteChaser, each new request gets an AI-drafted reply **within 60 seconds** that reads the quote lines, and open quotes get polite follow-ups until the buyer answers. A weekly report shows the **money left on the table**.
whyNow: AI can now write a context-aware reply (reading the quote lines and the customer's history) for a fraction of a cent, while most small sales teams still answer slowly. There is no regulatory deadline.
evidence: A 2025 study of 1,333 law firms found a 13-minute median response time, only 25% replying within 5 minutes, and 26% never replying [Focus Digital]
Only about 3% of teams respond to new leads within 5 minutes [Neil Patel]
The "100 times more likely to connect within 5 minutes" figure comes from an old MIT/InsideSales study (around 2007): a direction, not a fact [Verse.ai]
B2B QuoteAutomator leads quote intake on Shopify with 4.9 stars from 658 reviews [Shopify App Store]
SetuBridge's AI quote app starts at $7.99/month [eCommerce Guide]

whyReal.title: Slow replies are the norm
whyReal.text: In the law-firm study only 25% replied within 5 minutes and 26% never replied; across teams only about 3% reply within 5 minutes.

whyReal.title: Quote apps are popular
whyReal.text: B2B QuoteAutomator has 658 reviews on Shopify: stores clearly use quote forms. But intake is solved; follow-up is not.

whyReal.title: The pitch is simple
whyReal.text: Jonatan can say "you have €X of open quotes" after looking at a store's own export.

whyReal.title: Cheap to run
whyReal.text: Each AI message costs a fraction of a cent.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: B2B and wholesale online stores with "request a quote" forms, and small sales teams (2–10 reps) on HubSpot free/Starter or Pipedrive.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: The owner or head of sales.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: English-speaking B2B stores worldwide via the Shopify App Store and HubSpot App Marketplace.

solution.title: Connect the source
solution.text: Shopify draft orders, a WooCommerce quote plugin or a HubSpot form webhook.

solution.title: Instant AI reply
solution.text: a reply that reads the quote lines and customer history, within 60 seconds; approve-first or automatic mode.

solution.title: Follow-up cadence
solution.text: polite follow-ups that stop as soon as the buyer replies.

solution.title: Weekly report
solution.text: "money left on the table": value of open and lost quotes.

must: WooCommerce quote plugin or HubSpot form webhook
AI-drafted reply within 60 seconds (approve-first or automatic)
Follow-up cadence that stops on reply
Reply sorting (interested, price objection, not now)
Weekly "money left on the table" report

techStack: Shopify / WooCommerce / HubSpot APIs and webhooks
Small LLM for replies and classification
Transactional email with own sending domain (Postmark / Resend)

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Find 20 B2B Shopify or WooCommerce stores with "request a quote" buttons; ask for an export of the last 90 days of quotes; calculate the value of unconverted quotes; offer a hand-run pilot. Goal: 3 pilots at $49.
Victor builds the Shopify connection, AI reply drafting and follow-up cadence.
WooCommerce/HubSpot connection, reply sorting, weekly report, billing.
Shopify App Store listing; pilots move to paid plans.

costs.note: Small EU cloud server or Vercel/Supabase free tiers + transactional email (report estimate)
A fraction of a cent per message
Carrd / Typeform / Google Forms for the no-code test
Report estimate, not a price quote

risks.answer: Send from the store's own domain with proper SPF/DKIM/DMARC; low volume; stop on reply.

risks.risk: HubSpot and Shopify add native AI follow-up
risks.answer: Work across platforms and focus on B2B quotes, not generic sequences.
Stay in B2B quotes and wholesale stores, not home services.

questions: How many quotes or leads do you get per month, and what share convert?
Who follows up, how fast, and how many times?
What happened to the last quote that went silent?
What tools send your follow-ups today?
If we recovered 5% of unconverted quotes, what would that be worth to you?
